1. Criminal Case No. : 4087/2019 2. Date of commission of offense : In the year 2009 3. Date of institution of the case : 23.03.2019 4. Name of the complainant : State 5. Name of accused and parentage : Itender Khapra S/o Hardayal Khapra
6. Offense complained or proved : 420/468/471 IPC 7. Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty 8. Date on which order was reserved : 24.12.2025 9.
Final order : Acquitted 10. Date of final order : 26.12.2025 1. The accused is facing trial for offence u/s 420/468/471 IPC.

The genesis of the prosecution story is that in the year 2009 at unknown time at PHQ, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS IP Estate accused submitted form no. 10217 with forged DL No. 9069/MTR/05 issued from Transport Authority, Mathura, UP for the post of driver in Delhi Police and fraudulently and dishonestly induced the examining / appointing authority of Delhi Police to believe that the same was original /
genuine and on representation of accused, he was provisionally selected for the post of driver (Constable) in Delhi Police and also on the abovesaid date, time and place he used the forged DL No.
9069/MTR/05 as genuine which he knew or had reason to believe that the same was forged and thus committed an offence u/s 420/468/471 IPC.
Pursuant to the complaint made by the complainant, the criminal law was set into motion vide registration of the FIR against accused.

On completion of investigation, the present charge-sheet for offence u/s 420/468/471 IPC was filed against accused.
2. After taking the cognizance of the offence, the provisions of section 207 Cr.P.C. were complied with by supplying copy of charge-sheet and documents to accused.
Thereafter, on the basis of material on record, charges for offence u/s 420/511 IPC and 471 IPC were framed against accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
3. In order to establish the guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined 10 witnesses in all.

In brief, the testimonies of the material prosecution witnesses are discussed as under:
3.1 PW-1 Insp Anil Baudh deposed that since February 2017, he remained posted as Inspector/Incharge Recruitment Cell, PHQ, ITO, New Delhi.

On 03.04.2017, at the request of SI Amrish Giri IO, I.P.Estate Central Delhi, he provided the original application form No. 10217 of candidate Itender Khapra, documents/testimonial submitted by candidate and photocopy of his attendance sheet to him vide letter no.
1142/Rectt. Cell/AC-II, Dt. 03.04.2017.
This witness was partly examined in chief.
3.2 PW-2 SI Ludarmani deposed that he was working as Dealing Clerk at Recruitment Cell NPL Delhi since April 2021.
He brought the original record regarding the deployment for the duty of Invigilators in the examination conducted for the post of Constable (Driver) in Delhi Police at PTS Wazirabad.

As per the record the Candidate Itender Khapra having Roll No. 811898 had attended the examination vide arrangement ground-D North Side PTS Wazirabad in row no. 98 and SI Ashok Kumar, No. 4056/D had performed his duty as Invigilator there.
This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.
3.3 PW-2A Sh. V.A. Gupta (wrongly mentioned as PW-2) deposed that in the year 2013, he was posted as DCP, Land and Building, Delhi.
In the year 2009, vacancies for the post of Constable (driver) in Delhi Police were published in Leading Newspaper and Employment Newspaper.

In response to the advertisement, one candidate namely Itender Khapra S/o Sh. Har Dayal Khapra R/o VPO Nathupur, Dist. Sonipat, Haryana applied for the same against application form bearing number 10217 and the photocopy of the required educational certificate and driving license number 9069/MTR/05 for heavy vehicles were alleged to be issued from Agra Transport Authority valid upto 04.02.2011.

On scrutiny of the driving license, it was found that the driving license was not issued from Mathura Transport Authority to Itender Khapra and the same was found issued in the name of Sandeep Kumar Singh.
The candidate was provisionally selected for the said post.
The candidate Itender Khapra had applied for the post by submitting forged DL.
The matter was reported to DCP Central vide letter number 1001/Rectt.Cell/AC-II/PHQ dt. 04.02.2013.
This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.

3.4 PW-3 SI Kailash deposed that he brought summoned record i.e. file containing documents maintained by the Recruitment Cell in respect of candidate Itender Khapra who had applied for the State vs Itender Khapra on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79662119/
2 post of constable (driver) in Delhi Police in the year 2009.

The file contained the original DL verification report bearing no. 1190/License/Satyapan/2012 dated 18.05.2012, provisional result of candidates which included the name of accused Itender Khapra, employment newspaper dated 19.02.2009 and 21.02.2009 regarding publication of recruitment for the post of Ct. Driver,
attendance sheet, copy of application form and corresponding letters etc.

Copy of DL verification report bearing no. 1190/License/Satyapan/2012 dated 18.05.2012, Ex.PW3/A, result provisional of candidates which includes the name of accused Itender Khapra employment newspaper dated 19.02.2009 and 21.02.2009 regarding publication of recruitment for the post of Ct. Driver.
This witness was cross- examined by Ld. counsel for defence.
3.5 PW-5 SI Rakesh Kumar deposed that on 07.08.2013, he was posted at P.S. I.P.Estate as SI.
After registration of the FIR, the investigation was marked to him.
He received the case file and perused the same.
In this case, the alleged person was provisionally selected in Delhi police on the post of Constable driver but during verification the DL of accused/alleged person was found forged.
He was transferred and he handed over the case file to MHC(M).
This witness was not cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.
3.6 PW-5A ASI Rakesh Kumar(wrongly mentioned as PW-5) deposed that on 07.08.2013, he was posted at P.S. I.P.Estate as HC/DO from 09:00 am to 05:00 pm.
On that day, at about 01:30 pm, he received complaint under the signature of DCP V.A. Gupta duly forwarded by SHO P.S. I.P.Estate for registration of the FIR.
He registered the FIR through the then computer operator after making endorsement vide DD NO. 16A on rukka.
He issued a certificate u/s- 65 B Evidence Act in support of that FIR.

The copy of the FIR was retained as record in police station and one copy of FIR alongwith original complaint and certificate u/s- 65 B Evidence Act were handed over to SI Rakesh Kumar to whom the investigation was marked.
This witness was cross- examined by Ld. counsel for defence.
Yashpal Singh, Peon from the office of ARTO Mathura deposed that he was working as Peon at office of ARTO Mathura, U.P. since year 2008.

He had brought the summoned record i.e.
original DL issuing register of 2005.
As per record, the DL No. 9069/MTR/05 was issued to Sandeep Kumar Singh S/o Sh. Vishwanath Singh R/o 168, Nagla Bhutia, Mathura on 17.08.2005 for motor cycle and LMV.
As per record, the DL No. 9069/MTR/05 had not been issued in the name of Itender Khapra.
This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.

signatures and writings marked Q1 to Q2 on application form for recruitment, blue enclosed standards specimen signatures and writings and admitted signature on attendance sheet for written test for recruitment for constable male in Delhi Police of Itender Khapra were received in laboratory for examination in respect of case FIR no. 233/2013, P.S. All the documents were carefully and thoroughly examined with the help of scientific instruments under various lighting conditions and magnification, he opined that it had not been possible to express any opinion on red enclosed questioned signature and writing marked Q1 & Q2 in comparison to blue enclosed standard signatures and writings similarly stamped and marked S1 to S8 & A1.
However, further attempt could be made if more admitted signatures and writings of person concerned preferably of contemporary period might be procured and supplied to the laboratory for comparison.

3 was not cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.
3.9 PW-8 SI Sandeep Singh deposed that on 25.03.2017, he was posted at P.S. I.P.Estate as SI.
The further investigation of the case was marked to him.
He received the case file and perused the same.
In present matter, the previous IO/SI Amrish Giri had obtained the documents from Recruitment Cell PHQ, Delhi.
He served notice u/s- 41 Cr.P.C to accused Itender Khapra.
On 12.06.2018, accused joined investigation in response to the notice u/s- 41(a) Cr.P.C.
He made inquiry from accused and thereafter, he bound down the accused.
The specimen handwriting and signature of accused were obtained on several papers which were given as S1 to S8.
In present matter the, DL question of accused Itender Khapra was issued from the office of ARTO, Mathura, U.P.
On 19.06.2018, he served notice u/s- 91 Cr.P.C at the office of District Transport Officer, Mathura Authority, U.P. to produce the necessary information/document detailed mentioned in his notice.
He received the DL verification report bearing no. 2126/Licence/Satyapan/2018 dated 20.04.2018 address to him and he placed the same on record.
As per DL verification report, the DL number 9069/MTR/05 was not issued to accused Itender Khapra S/o Hardyal Khapra from the office of ARTO, Mathura, U.P.
He recorded the statement of invigilator.
The exhibits i.e. admitted signatures of accused on application form and attendance sheet and specimen handwriting and signature were sent to FSL, Rohini for examination.
The statement of witnesses were recorded.
Chagesheet was filed requesting to file supplementary chargesheet on receiving FSL report.

This witness was cross-examined by Ld.
counsel for defence.
3.10 PW-9 Mohd. Ibrahim deposed that in the year-2018, he was working as Senior Assistant at ARTO, Mathura, U.P.

He prepared the report, wherein the report stated that license no.
9069/MTR/05 was not issued in the name of Itender Khapra S/o Sh. Hardyal Khapra.
This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence.

4. After prosecution evidence, the statement of accused u/s 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded, wherein all the incriminating circumstances were offered to accused to which accused stated that he has been falsely implicated.
He further stated that the DL bearing no. 9069/MTR/05 was genuine and was issued by office of ARTO Mathura.
Thereafter, accused did not lead evidence in his defence.
5. Thereafter, matter was fixed for final arguments.
6. Ld.
APP for State has contended that the prosecution has proved its case beyond all reasonable doubts and therefore, the accused is liable to be convicted for offence u/s 420/511 and 471 IPC.
7. Per contra, Ld.
Defence counsel for accused has vehemently argued that the prosecution has failed to establish guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
It is argued that the verification report on the basis of which prosecution was initiated against accused has not been proved as the authors of the reports have not deposed.
With these submissions, prayer is made for acquittal of accused from the alleged offences.

8. Having discussed the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, the following issues emerge for our consideration:-

1. Whether the action of accused constitute the offence of cheating u/s 420 IPC.
2. Whether accused forged the driving license punishable u/s 471 IPC.

Analysis:
The Hon'ble Supereme Court of India in Mariam Fasihuddin & Anr. Vs. State by Adugodi Police Station & Anr. Crl. Apeal no. 335/2024 observed The offence of cheating under Section 420 IPC :
10. Section 420 IPC provides that whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy, the whole or any part of valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be liable to be punished for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

entities.text: Mariam Fasihuddin & Anr. Vs. State by Adugodi Police Station & Anr. Crl. Apeal no. 335/2024
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, Section 415 IPC distinctly defines the term'cheating'.

The provision elucidates that an act marked by fraudulent or dishonest intentions will be categorised as 'cheating' if it is intended to induce the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property,
causing damage or harm to that person.

11.It is thus paramount that in order to attract the provisions of Section 420 IPC, the prosecution has to not only prove that the accused has cheated someone but also that by doing so, he has dishonestly induced the person who is cheated to deliver property.

There are, thus, three components of this offence, i.e., (I) the deception 10 P a g e of any person, (ii) fraudulently or dishonestly inducing that person to deliver any property to any person, and (iii) mensrea or dishonest intention of the accused at the time of making the inducement.
There is no gainsaid that for the offence of cheating, fraudulent and dishonest intention must exist from the inception when the promise or representation was made.
12.It is well known that every deceitful act is not unlawful, just as not every unlawful act is deceitful.
Some acts may be termed both as unlawful as well as deceitful, and such acts alone will fall within the purview of Section 420 IPC.

It must also be understood that a statement of fact is deemed 'deceitful' when it is false, and is knowingly or recklessly made with the intent that it shall be acted upon by another person, resulting in damage or loss.2 'Cheating' therefore, generally involves a preceding deceitful act that dishonestly induces a person to deliver any property or any part of a valuable security, prompting the induced person to undertake the said act, which they would not have done but for the inducement.
13.Theterm 'property' employed in Section 420 IPC has a well defined connotation.
Every species of valuable right or interest that is subject to ownership and has an exchangeable value-is ordinarily understood as 'property'.

It also describes one's State vs Itender Khapra on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79662119/
5 exclusive right to possess, use and dispose of a thing.

The IPC itself defines the term 2 P. Ramanatha Aiyar, Advanced Law Lexicon, 6th Edition, Vol. 1, pg.903. 11| P a g e 'moveable property' as, "intended to include corporeal property of every description,
except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth."
Whereas immoveable property is generally understood to mean land, benefits arising out of land and things attached or permanently fastened to the earth.

The offence of forgery under Sections 468 and 471 IPC: 21.The offence of 'forgery' under Section 468 IPC postulates that whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic document forged, shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Whereas Section 471 IPC states that whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any documents which he knows or has reason to believe it 15 | P a g e to be a forged document, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document.

22.There are two primary components that need to be fulfilled in order to establish the offence of 'forgery', namely: (I) that the accused has fabricated an instrument;
and (ii) it was done with the intention that the forged document would be used for the purpose of cheating.
Simply put, the offence of forgery requires the preparation of a false document with the dishonest intention of causing damage or injury.
23.The
offences of 'forgery' and 'cheating' intersect and converge, as the act of forgery is committed with the intent to deceive or cheat an individual.
Having extensively addressed the aspect of dishonest intent in the context of 'cheating' under Section 420 IPC, it stands established that no dishonest intent can be made out against the Appellants.

Our focus therefore will now be confined,
for the sake of brevity, to the first element, i.e.,the preparation of a false document.
The determination of whether the Appellants prepared a false document, by forging Respondent No. 2's signature, however, cannot be even prima facie ascertained at this juncture.
Considering the primary ingredient of dishonest intention itself could not be established against the Appellants, the offence of forgery too, has no legs to stand.
It is also significant to highlight that the proceedings as against the concerned Passport Officer, who was implicated as Accused No. 4, already stand quashed.
In such like situation and coupled with the nature of allegations, we are unable to appreciate as to why the Appellants be subjected to the ordeal of trial.

9. The case of prosecution as per original complaint Ex. PW2/A is that accused applied for the vacancies of Constable(driver) upon the strength of the heavy driving license no. 9069/MTR/2005 issued from ARTO Mathura on 16.08.2005 having its validity upto 04.02.2011 but upon the verification, the DL was not found issued and found not valid upon the basis of letter no.
1190/license satyapan/2012 dated 18.05.2012.
In the trial, PW-2A complainant proved the original complaint Ex. PW2/A by identifying his signatures upon the complaint and affirming the version of complaint.

State vs Itender Khapra on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79662119/
6 10.
During the trial, the prosecution was required to prove both the verification reports on the basis of which the charge-sheet was filed against accused.
The original verification report No. 1190/license satyapan/2012 dated 18.05.2012 has not been exhibited by the prosecution in the trial.
Even the author who prepared the aforestated verification report has not been examined by the prosecution.
There is another verification report issued during the investigation, bearing no. 2126/license satyapan/2018 dated 20.06.2018 Ex. PW8/C.

This report remarks that the license bearing no.
9069/MTR/2005 was not issued.
It is further remarked that the aforestated license was found to be fake.
The prosecution was required to prove that both the verification reports were prepared from the original record available in the ARTO Office, Mathura.
However, in the verification report dated 18.05.2012, it is remarked that the license was found to be issued to one Sandeep Kumar Singh S/o Vishwanath Singh.
Contrarily, Ex. PW8/C, another verification report reflects that such license number was never issued.

The subsequent verification report Ex.
PW8/C is contradictory to the previous verification report as the contradictory stand has been taken by ARTO Mathura.

If that was the case that no such licence number was issued, PW-6 Yashpal Singh could not have brought the original DL issuing register as per which the DL no. 9069/MTR/05 was issued to some other person.

11. PW-6 Yashpal Singh brought the original DL issuing register of year 2005 as per which the DL number 9069/MTR/05 was issued to one Sh. Sandeep Kumar Singh S/o Sh. Vishwanath Singh on 17.08.2005 for motorcycle and LMV.

However, when the licence was already issued to some other person, no such report stating that the licence number was not issued at all, could have been prepared but the report was sent by ARTO, Mathura in year 2018 by stating that no such licence was issued at all.
The report should have remarked that the licence was issued to some other person.
Meaning thereby, that the verification report was not prepared after going through the original record available at ARTO, Mathura.
12. Furthermore, PW-6 Yashpal who brought the original record was not record keeper and was merely a peon and did not file any authority to produce the record.
He did not have any control over the original record being a peon.
Further, the record was not handed over to him through any authorization letter which further weakens the case of prosecution.
The author of verification report Ex. PW8/C did not step into the witness box and PW-9 Mohd. Ibrahim appeared in the witness who co-authored the verification report Ex. PW8/C.
In his examination in chief, he deposed that he prepared the report Ex. PW8/C but in the cross-examination, he stated that he signed the verification report on the behest of Ms. Babita.
He further admitted that he did not prepare the report and he merely signed on the report.
He further expressed his ignorance on the question whether the report was prepared after perusing the record.
Ms. Babita did not come for deposition and Ex. PW8/C remained unproved.
Both the verification reports could not be proved by the prosecution.

13. The moot question is when the original record reflects that the impugned license was issued to some other person, the verification report Ex. PW8/C stating that the license number was not issued at all, could not have been prepared.

The aforesaid contradiction was not clarified by the maker of the verification report indicating that either the original record is questionable or the verification State vs Itender Khapra on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79662119/
7 report Ex. PW8/C was prepared without considering the original record.
Further, Ex. PW8/B is notice issued u/s 91 Cr.PC to ARTO Mathura asking various questions in respect of the impugned license to which reply Ex. PW8/C was sent by ARTO Mathura.
It is to be noted that ARTO Mathura did not answer to any of the questions asked by IO through notice u/s 91 Cr.PC.
A three word report was sent by ARTO Mathura stating that " jari nahi hai".
The conduct of ARTO Mathura is questionable in this regard.
The other queries posed by IO vide Ex. PW8/B were not addressed at all by ARTO official for reason best known to her.
More surprisingly, PW-8 IO SI Sandeep did not take any other action against the officials of ARTO Mathura for not providing the information which was repeatedly sought by the IO.
PW-8 IO SI Sandeep admitted that he did not record the statement of ARTO officials.
There is no explanation as to why the ARTO officials were not interrogated even when they did not reply to the notice issued by IO in detail.

14. Another aspect to be considered is that verification report dated 18.05.2012 also reflects that the license was not issued to accused but the signatory of the report has not been examined by the prosecution.

Examination of author of the report dated 18.05.2012 could have been beneficial for the prosecution but the IO did not even mention the name of the person who signed on original report dated 18.05.2012, upon the basis of which FIR was registered.
15. It is the settled law that it is the duty of the prosecution to prove the case beyond reasonable doubts, the burden of proof can never be shifted to the defence.

In the present matter, prosecution had to prove that accused with dishonest intention got the forged DL issued in his favour and tried to cause wrongful loss to the complainant but as discussed in the previous paras, prosecution could not prove that the DL no. 9069/MTR/05 was not issued in the name of accused and accused had knowledge that DL No. 9069/MTR/05 was not genuine and despite knowing, he used the DL while applying for the vacancies.
The authors of the verification report never deposed before the court.
The alleged forged DL was never sent to FSL to show that it was fraudulently prepared.

16. As an outcome of the discussion made above, this Court is of the view that the answers to the issues framed at S.No. 1 and 2 are in negative and prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubts and benefit of doubt must be given to the accused .

Accordingly, accused Itender Khapra is acquitted for offences u/s 420/511/471 IPC.
17.
The bail bonds furnished by accused at the commencement of trial, stands cancelled.
Sureties stands discharged.
The bail bonds furnished by accused persons u/s 437A Cr.PC. shall remain in force for a period of six months or till the statutory period to assail this judgment expires (whichever is earlier).
Documents, if any be returned to its rightful owner in accordance with rules.
Endorsement, if any, also stands cancelled.
Case property shall be disposed off after expiration of period for filing appeal and in case of appeal, as per direction of Ld. Appellate Court.
Case stands disposed off.
File be consigned to record room after due completion.

In the present matter, prosecution had to prove that accused with dishonest intention got the forged DL issued in his favour and tried to cause wrongful loss to the complainant but as discussed in the previous paras, prosecution could not prove that the DL no. 9069/MTR/05 was not issued in the name of accused and accused had knowledge that DL No. 9069/MTR/05 was not genuine and despite knowing, he used the DL while applying for the vacancies.
The authors of the verification report never deposed before the court.
The alleged forged DL was never sent to FSL to show that it was fraudulently prepared.
16. As an outcome of the discussion made above, this Court is of the view that the answers to the issues framed at S.No. 1 and 2 are in negative and prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubts and benefit of doubt must be given to the accused .
